text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Thursday.

GERMANY - Bund futures posted solid gains after hopes for a repo cut were fanned by comments from Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp and a Bundesbank report predicting little threat from inflation.
The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.65, up 0.35 from Wednesday's settlement price.
BRITAIN - UK gilt futures ended nearly a full point firmer after December retail price inflation fell back and Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke left interest rates unchanged.
The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 110-21/32, up 24/32 from Wednesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures posted a new contract high for the second day running as hopes for interest rate cuts in Europe boosted debt markets, overshadowing some disappointment the Bank of France failed to trim rates.
The March bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 130.62, up 0.40. from Wednesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bond futures eased back in early trading on further profit taking after the market hit fresh record levels early on Wednesday and also reflecting the lower close on U.S. T-bonds overnight.
The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 131.00 up 0.38 from Wednesday's settlement price.
UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasury prices opened higher, in line with overseas trends, as the market waited for weekly data on U.S. jobless claims.
The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 111-4/32, down 5/32 from Wednesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.8 percent.
JAPAN - The key March Japanese government bond futures contract ended higher on Thursday, as buying of cash JGBs by investors led to a flurry of short-covering.
November machinery orders data, released in the afternoon, came within market expectations and had little effect on the market.
In after hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 126.18, up 0.59 from Wednesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
EUROBONDS - LONDON - A broad range of new issues were launched during a busy Eurobond session.
DSL Bank launched a $300 millon four-year deal at 12 b.p. over, and Rabobank set a $150 million four-year issue at a five b.p. spread.
